doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Is the San Francisco jazz scene as active as the listings suggest
summary: Lateano says the scene is real but listings include restaurant wallpaper music; he moved here in 1966 on his way elsewhere and stayed.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well people say that. They come in and just like what you’re saying, it can be deceiving. There is an active jazz scene. First I should say that. I mean there are a lot of people here that make their living playing jazz. But the listings sometimes, you have several listings and it might be music in a restaurant, which could be jazz but also could be wallpaper. And we’ve all been there, and there is a difference. I say the same thing, I have a friend that lives in Los Angeles and I’ve seen the Los Angeles newspaper and I say man, there’s really a lot going on. He says well, I don’t know. He says the same thing. But it’s a vibrant scene, I mean you can make a living here.

Exactly. That’s why I’m here. Because when I moved here, oh 35 years ago I guess, ’66, I was on my way somewhere else. I mean I’d just got out of the service you know, I was visiting friends here and I thought well I’ll go to L.A. or New York, I mean that’s where the music business is. And I got here and I just started hanging out and playing and I thought, you know I really like the climate and the town and the people, it just really appeals to me. And I just kept staying here and staying here and here I am. But I hooked up with bands and traveled and everything. So you can make a living here.
